evidence: A traveler calls the AE1200 the perfect choice, citing its ten-year battery and low replacement cost after three years of happy ownership.

evidence_sources.author: al_borland
evidence_sources.excerpt: I then stumbled across the Casio AE1200, their world timer. As I thought about it, this was the perfect choice. With a 10 year battery, I could just grab it and go (changing the battery whenever I renew my passport), I didn't have to deal with setting a bunch of complications, because the quartz movement just kept it going all the time. It solved the IST problem. The low cost meant that I could travel without having to worry about my watch... if something happened, oh well, get another one. Along with that, I wouldn't make me a target for pickpockets. I had been so caught up in watch culture that I didn't realize being cheap could be a feature in the right context. I've had it for about 3 years now and still smile every time I wear it.
